reading: The few cells in one corner are completed into a pattern with four-fold symmetry about the grid centre; where a ring's corner cell has a neighbouring mark two cells along the ring, that mark's colour is repeated on every other cell along the ring's edges between the mirrored corners.

slots.symmetry: mirror about both grid centre lines (and the diagonal)
slots.dotted_edges: for each ring whose corner has an adjacent-by-2 mark of colour c, every second cell of the ring's four edges between its corners becomes c

why: output is symmetric about both centre lines; every ring with a side mark has a full alternating dotted edge of that mark colour

reading: A partially drawn symmetric pattern is completed so that the output is symmetric about both its horizontal and vertical centre lines.
why: the output is mirror-symmetric left-right and top-bottom; every input fg cell is kept

reading: The big rectangle is projected outward to the grid border in all four directions as full-width bands, but any single row or column of a band that contains a scattered marker is left out entirely; markers stay.

slots.subject: the large solid rectangle (largest object)
slots.lanes: each row (left/right) and column (up/down) of the rectangle's span, from its edge to the grid border
slots.rule: a lane is painted with the rectangle colour only if it contains no marker; blocked lanes stay unchanged

why: every lane from the rectangle to the border is either fully rectangle-coloured (no marker in it) or untouched (contains a marker)
invariants: cells outside the rectangle's row and column spans

reading: A background cell becomes 4 when four 2-cell segments of colour 1 point at it from left, right, above and below, each with a one-cell gap.

new_rows.name: cross_centre
new_rows.datalog: cross_centre(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 8), XL2 = X - 2, XL3 = X - 3, XR2 = X + 2, XR3 = X + 3, YU2 = Y - 2, YU3 = Y - 3, YD2 = Y + 2, YD3 = Y + 3, px(Y, XL2, 1), px(Y, XL3, 1), px(Y, XR2, 1), px(Y, XR3, 1), px(YU2, X, 1), px(YU3, X, 1), px(YD2, X, 1), px(YD3, X, 1).

why: exactly the cells with colour-1 cells at distances 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions become 4

reading: Inside a 7 rectangle a 2 cell has a tail of 6s; a ray from the 2 continues away from the tail through the 7 interior, and the first frame cell it reaches is recoloured 7.

slots.head: the single 2 cell
slots.direction: from the adjacent 6 toward the 2 (orthogonal or diagonal)
slots.path: cells of colour 7 passed through unchanged
slots.target: first non-7 cell on the ray (in the outer frame), recoloured 7

why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 opposite its 6 tail, and it becomes 7

reading: Each 2 that lies inside a 3 rectangle gets a 3x3 ring of 1 drawn around it (overwriting whatever is there, even outside the rectangle); 2s lying in the 0 background get nothing.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
orth4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth4(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
nb3(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, 2), off(DY, DX), orth4(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, 3).
anchor(Y, X) :- nb3(Y, X, N), N > 1.
halo(Y, X) :- anchor(AY, AX), off(DY, DX), Y = AY + DY, X = AX + DX, px(Y, X, C), !anchor(Y, X).

why: every 8-neighbour of a 2 having at least two orthogonal 3-neighbours becomes 1, except such 2s themselves; nothing else changes
invariants: 3 cells not adjacent to an anchor

reading: The grid is a lattice of identical framed 2x2 tiles; when two tiles in the same tile-row or tile-column carry the same odd colour at the same sub-position, every tile between them gets that colour at that sub-position.

slots.cells: the framed 2x2 tiles of the lattice
slots.mark: a sub-position value differing from the common value at that sub-position
slots.rule: two equal marks in one tile-row or tile-column fill all tiles between them with that mark at the same sub-position

why: for every sub-position, marks of one colour form unbroken runs between the two original marks along tile-rows/columns

reading: The right column and bottom row carry matching runs of colours; each colour c fills the block where its rows in the right column cross its columns in the bottom row.

slots.row_key: right column: colour of each row
slots.col_key: bottom row: colour of each column
slots.rule: cell (y,x) becomes c when right_column[y] = bottom_row[x] = c

why: every cell whose row key equals its column key takes that colour; all others stay

reading: The input is copied twice side by side.
why: output is a 1x2 arrangement of exact input copies

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.

slots.extent: k x k blocks, k = number of distinct colours in the input

why: every output block is the input, and the block count per side equals the input's distinct colour count
